book_titles: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: Why does a time-horizon jump from 3 minutes to 30 minutes represent a smaller increase in AI difficulty than a jump from 30 minutes to 5 hours, despite both being 10x multipliers?

checklist.criterion: Does the response explain that the fitted spline is nearly flat in the 2–30 minute range?
Does the response state that the model is close to linear outside of the 2–30 minute range?
Does the response claim that the difficulty is perfectly linear across all time scales?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: Compare the 'equal-task' and 'equal-family' weighting schemes used for evaluating AI performance. How do their targets differ?

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that equal-task weighting targets a uniformly drawn task?
Does the response state that equal-family weighting targets a uniformly drawn task family?
Does the response suggest that these schemes weight the tasks differently than the AIs?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: What are the specific components used to model the latent difficulty $\theta_i$ in the item-response theory framework?

checklist.criterion: Does the response include a mean function $f$ of $\log_2 T_i$?
Does the response include a family variance $\tau$?
Does the response include an idiosyncratic variance $\sigma$?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: Explain the purpose of the correlation parameter $\rho$ and the derived parameter $\phi$ in the overdispersion model.

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that $\rho$ is shared among all AIs?
Does the response define $\phi$ as $(1-\rho)/\rho$?
Does the response explain that this allows for higher variance than a standard binomial model?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: How does the spline-based approach differ from the standard assumption regarding the relationship between AI difficulty and human completion time?

checklist.criterion: Does the response identify the standard assumption as a linear dependence on the log of human time?
Does the response state that the spline model relaxes this linear assumption?
Does the response state that the spline model is only used for tasks under 30 minutes?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: What numerical methods are employed to implement the maximum likelihood estimation for the overdispersion model?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention the use of an EM algorithm?
Does the response mention the use of Gauss-Hermite quadrature?
Does the response state that the likelihood is invariant to affine transformations of $\theta$?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: What is the core principle behind anchoring AI capability in human completion time within the context of item-response theory?

checklist.criterion: Does the response explain that human time serves as a covariate?
Does the response state that this allows capability to be measured in interpretable units?
Does the response state that this method eliminates the need for any external data?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: Define 'overdispersion' in the context of AI-task success indicators and explain why it is modeled using a Beta-binomial distribution.

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that overdispersion accounts for correlation between trials for the same AI-task pair?
Does the response state that the Beta-binomial model allows for higher variance than a binomial model?
Does the response state that the correlation $\rho$ is unique to every individual task?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: How does the 'sqrt-family' weighting scheme relate to the 'equal-task' and 'equal-family' schemes?

checklist.criterion: Does the response describe 'sqrt-family' as an intermediate weighting scheme?
Does the response state that all three schemes weight the AIs uniformly?
Does the response state that 'sqrt-family' targets a uniformly drawn task family?

questions.book_title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
questions.query: What diagnostic measures are suggested to ensure the construct validity of AI time horizons as benchmarks grow or include longer tasks?

checklist.criterion: Does the response suggest interpreting time horizons together with diagnostic plots?
Does the response mention using these plots to assess construct validity?
Does the response suggest that diagnostic plots are only necessary for tasks under 30 minutes?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: What are the three distinct settings used to evaluate agentic LEGO-set design in the BrickBench framework?

checklist.criterion: Does the response identify the 'Model' setting as having a part limit of ≤400?
Does the response identify the 'Set' setting as having a part range of 400–4000?
Does the response identify the 'Alt-Build' setting as being restricted to the part inventory of set 10698?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: Describe the core functionality and specific tools provided by the BrickAgent environment.

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention the inclusion of the LDraw library and the BrickNet connector system?
Does the response list tools for searching, placing, mirroring, measuring, defining subassemblies, and rendering?
Does the response state that the environment includes a validator for connectivity, collision, and stability?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: How does the availability of the BrickAgent toolset affect the performance of frontier coding agents in constructing valid builds?

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that agents without these tools cannot reliably construct valid builds?
Does the response state that agents with the tools can satisfy physical and semantic requirements?
Does the response claim that agents without tools still achieve high validity scores?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: What specific physics parameters are applied in the PyBullet simulation to ensure that inter-component contacts do not slide or bounce?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention a high coefficient of friction?
Does the response mention no restitution?
Does the response state that components are simulated as single rigid bodies of uniform density?
Does the response mention a low coefficient of friction?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: What are the three primary reasons for an assembly being classified as invalid in the reference set?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention failures on stability?
Does the response mention failures on collisions?
Does the response mention failures on part requirements?
Does the response state that 'aesthetic' failures are a primary reason for invalidity?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: Contrast the 'Model' and 'Alt-Build' settings in terms of part quantity and inventory constraints.

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that 'Model' is limited to ≤400 parts?
Does the response state that 'Alt-Build' is restricted to the inventory of set 10698?
Does the response state that 'Alt-Build' allows for any number of parts?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: How is the VQA score calculated to measure the semantic alignment between a rendered assembly and a text prompt?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention rendering the assembly from eight views?
Does the response mention using Gemma 4 31B to judge the views?
Does the response mention asking each question of the graph in one call?
Does the response state that the VQA score is determined by human judgment?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: What is the relationship between the ELO score and the cost per build as observed in the benchmark summary?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention that ELO is plotted against mean assembly cost?
Does the response mention that agents are given a budget of 300 turns per prompt?
Does the response state that cost is the only factor determining ELO?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: What is the specific part count range for the 'Set' evaluation setting?

checklist.criterion: Does the response state the range is 400–4000 parts?
Does the response state the range is 100–1000 parts?

questions.book_title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
questions.query: How does the benchmark differentiate between the physical feasibility of a LEGO assembly and its semantic alignment with a user prompt?

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that validity is determined by collision-free and stability tests?
Does the response state that semantic alignment is measured using VQA scores?
Does the response state that Design ELO measures physical stability?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: What is the 'strong Allee effect' in the context of AI agent populations and how does it differ from independent agent growth?

checklist.criterion: Does the response explain that the strong Allee effect refers to a critical population threshold where growth becomes positive only above a certain size?
Does the response state that this effect is driven by collaboration increasing collective capability with population size?
Does the response claim that independent agents exhibit a population-dependent growth threshold?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: Contrast the growth boundaries of independent AI agents versus collaborative AI agents in terms of their dependence on population size (N).

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that for independent agents, the growth boundary depends on individual capability but is independent of population size N?
Does the response state that for collaborative agents, the growth boundary depends on population size N?
Does the response suggest that increasing N always increases the growth rate for independent agents?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: What is the mathematical definition of the critical success probability (qcrit) and the critical population threshold (Ncrit)?

checklist.criterion: Does the response identify qcrit as the ratio of the loss fraction (mu) to the growth constant (kappa)?
Does the response provide the formula for Ncrit involving Nref, pref, pcrit, and beta?
Does the response state that qcrit is a function of population size N?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: Define 'ecological safety' and explain how it differs from standard multi-agent safety.

checklist.criterion: Does the response define ecological safety as concerning the dynamics of the population itself rather than a fixed population?
Does the response mention that it addresses the risk of a self-reinforcing cycle of population expansion?
Does the response state that ecological safety only concerns the safety of a single agent's actions?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: How does the relationship between search depth (d) and computational cost (C) influence the success probability (p) in a collaborative model?
questions.context_hint: Search depth, cost, and success probability

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that success probability p(d) follows a model of diminishing returns as depth increases?
Does the response state that computational cost C(d) grows exponentially with search depth d?
Does the response state that cost C(d) decreases as depth d increases?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: Describe the mathematical model for success probability p(d) relative to a reference depth dref.

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention the use of an exponential decay of the failure probability?
Does the response identify the parameter rho as the control for how strongly success probability increases with depth?
Does the response state that the model assumes a linear increase in success probability with depth?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: Why is red teaming a small group of agents insufficient to guarantee ecological safety in a collaborative AI population?

checklist.criterion: Does the response explain that a small population may be below the critical threshold Ncrit?
Does the response state that a larger population of the same model could trigger a takeoff due to collaboration?
Does the response claim that red teaming a small group guarantees safety for any population size?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: Explain the mechanism of the population dynamics equation tau dN/dt = N(kappa * p(N) - mu).

checklist.criterion: Does the response identify kappa as the average number of units added per successful attempt?
Does the response identify mu as the fraction of existing units lost over time?
Does the response state that the population grows only when the success probability p(N) is greater than the critical probability qcrit?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: How does the success probability p(N) in a collaborative model scale relative to the reference population Nref?

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that p(N) increases as N increases?
Does the response mention the use of a power-law-like term (N/Nref)^-beta to model the failure probability?
Does the response state that p(N) decreases as N increases?

questions.book_title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
questions.query: What are the primary factors that contribute to the risk of a 'population explosion' of misaligned AI agents?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention the ability of agents to conduct real-world cyberattacks?
Does the response mention the ability to scale capabilities with the number of agents?
Does the response mention the collective pursuit of misaligned goals to obtain rewards?
Does the response state that the risk is primarily due to individual agent hardware failure?

Does the response state the copyright factor correlates with the contextual factor at 0.603?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: What is the primary reason for preferring the 3D standard/contextual/copyright structure over the 7D harm-domain model?

checklist.criterion: Does the response mention that the 3D model is more parsimonious?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: Compare the correlation patterns of non-copyright harm domains against the copyright domain within the 7D harm-domain model.

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that non-copyright harm domains are generally more tightly correlated (0.65 to 0.85)?
Does the response state that the copyright domain correlates lower (0.34 to 0.64) against other domains?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: What specific metrics were used as the primary and secondary criteria for evaluating held-out prediction accuracy across the 80/20 splits?

Does the response identify Brier score as the secondary check?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: Why does a single average score for a safety benchmark like HarmBench potentially mislead the assessment of a model's specific safety attributes?

checklist.criterion: Does the response explain that models with similar overall scores can have very different attribute profiles?
Does the response state that a single score isolates a single attribute like harmful refusal?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: How does the analysis distinguish between a model's behavior regarding copyright items and its behavior regarding other harm domains?

Does the response state that copyright reproduction is driven by the same refusal logic as other harms?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
questions.query: Contrast the role of 'standard' and 'contextual' factors in the 3D model with the 'copyright' factor.

checklist.criterion: Does the response state that standard and contextual factors correlate highly (0.785)?
Does the response state that the copyright factor correlates less strongly with these two factors?

questions.book_title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
